source_text:
Φοβήθητι, φησί, τὸν κύριον καὶ φύλασσε τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ. φυλάσσων οὖν τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ θεοῦ ἔσῃ δυνατὸς ἐν πάσῃ πράξει, καὶ ἡ πρᾶξίς σου ἀσύγκριτος ἔσται. φοβούμενος γὰρ τὸν κύριον πάντα καλῶς ἐργάσῃ: οὗτος δέ ἐστιν ὁ φόβος, ὃν δεῖ σε φοβηθῆναι, καὶ σωθῆναι.
τὸν δὲ διάβολον μὴ φοβηθῇς: φοβούμενος γὰρ τὸν κύριον κατακυριεύσεις τοῦ διαβόλου, ὅτι δύναμις ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν. ἐν ᾧ δὲ δύναμις οὐκ ἔστιν, οὐδὲ φόβος: ἐν ᾧ δὲ δύναμις ἡ ἔνδοξος, καὶ φόβος ἐν αὐτῷ. πᾶς γὰρ ὁ δύναμιν ἔχων φόβον ἔχει: ὁ δὲ μὴ ἔχων δύναμιν ὑπὸ πάντων καταφρονεῖται.
φοβήθητι δὲ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ διαβόλου, ὅτι πονηρά ἐστι. φοβούμενος οὖν τὸν κύριον οὐκ ἐργάσῃ αὐτά, ἀλλ’ ἀφέξῃ ἀπ’ αὐτῶν.
δισσοὶ οὖν εἰσιν οἱ φόβοι: ἐὰν γὰρ θέλῃς τὸ πονηρὸν ἐργάσασθαι, φοβοῦ τὸν κύριον, καὶ οὐκ ἐργάσῃ αὐτό: ἐὰν δὲ θέλῃς πάλιν τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἐργάσασθαι, φοβοῦ τὸν κύριον, καὶ ἐργάσῃ αὐτό. ὥστε ὁ φόβος τοῦ κυρίου ἰσχυρός ἐστι καὶ μέγας καὶ ἔνδοξος. φοβήθητι οὖν τὸν κύριον, καὶ ζήσῃ αὐτῷ: καὶ ὅσοι ἂν φοβηθῶσιν αὐτὸν καὶ τηρήσωσι τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ, ζήσονται τῷ θεῷ.
Διατί, φημί, κύριε, εἶπας περὶ τῶν τηρούντων τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ: Ζήσονται τῷ θεῷ; Ὅτι, φησίν, πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις φοβεῖται τὸν κύριον τὰς δὲ ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ οὐ φυλάσσει. τῶν οὖν φοβουμένων αὐτὸν καὶ φυλασσόντων τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ, ἐκείνων ἡ ζωή ἐστι παρὰ τῷ θεῷ: τῶν δὲ μὴ φυλασσόντων τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ, οὐδὲ ζωὴ ἐν αὐτῷ.
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the seventh commandment: fear the Lord and keep his commandments, but do not fear the devil, who has no power.
pass_a_gloss: Fear, he says, the Lord and keep the commandments of him. Keeping therefore the commandments of God you will be powerful in every deed, and the deed of you incomparable will be. Fearing for the Lord all things well you will do: this but is the fear, which it is necessary you to fear, and to be saved. The but devil do not fear: fearing for the Lord you will rule over the devil, because power in him not is. In whom but power not is, neither fear: in whom but power the glorious, also fear in him. Every for the [one] power having fear has: the but not having power by all is despised. Fear but the works of the devil, because evil they are. Fearing therefore the Lord not you will do them, but you will hold back from them. Twofold therefore are the fears: if for you wish the evil to do, fear the Lord, and not you will do it: if but you wish again the good to do, fear the Lord, and you will do it. So that the fear of the Lord strong is and great and glorious. Fear therefore the Lord, and you will live to him: and as many as would fear him and keep the commandments of him, they will live to God. Why, I say, lord, did you say about the [ones] keeping the commandments of him: They will live to God? Because, he says, all the creation fears the Lord, the but commandments of him not it keeps. Of the therefore fearing him and keeping the commandments of him, of those the life is with God: of the but not keeping the commandments of him, neither life in him.

choices.why: The adjective means 'beyond comparison'; 'incomparable' preserves the force that no other deed can be set beside it.
The compound verb means to gain mastery over; 'rule over' keeps the sense of dominion rather than mere victory.
The adjective marks the fears as two distinct kinds; 'twofold' preserves the dual nature without implying a pair of equal items.
The dative expresses living in relation to God; 'live to him' keeps the dative force rather than flattening it to 'live for God'.

pass_b_english: “Fear the Lord,” the Shepherd said, “and keep his commandments. If you keep the commandments of God, you will be powerful in every deed, and what you do will be beyond compare. For when you fear the Lord, you will do everything well. This is the fear you must have in order to be saved.

“But do not fear the devil. For if you fear the Lord, you will master the devil, because there is no power in him. One who has no power inspires no fear. But one who has glorious power inspires fear as well. For everyone who has power is feared, and the one who has no power is despised by all.
“But do fear the works of the devil, because they are evil. If you fear the Lord, you will not do them. You will keep away from them.

“So there are two kinds of fear. If you want to do evil, fear the Lord, and you will not do it. If, on the other hand, you want to do good, fear the Lord, and you will do it. So the fear of the Lord is strong and great and glorious. Fear the Lord, then, and you will live to him. And all who fear him and keep his commandments will live to God.”

“Sir,” I said, “why did you say of those who keep his commandments, ‘They will live to God’?” “Because,” he said, “all creation fears the Lord, but it does not keep his commandments. So life with God belongs to those who fear him and keep his commandments. But those who do not keep his commandments have no life in him.”

problems.why: "ἐν αὐτῷ" refers to God (in him), not "in them"; changes agency and meaning.
problems.ruling: ἐν αὐτῷ is singular ('in him'=God), but English 'in them' is plural, changing the referent and meaning.
